hazard: Lack of dedicated substance misuse team in police custody
theme: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

reports.title: Wayne Broad
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

promises.quote: The responsibility for healthcare in police custody suites will however soon transfer from individual police authorities to NHS England. Healthcare for persons in police custody will therefore be commissioned to NHS standards of care. This should lead to more consistent and improved healthcare standards, by ensuring that the same range and quality of substance misuse services are available to persons in police custody as would be available in prison or community settings.
promises.summary: Transfer custody healthcare to NHS England to standardise substance misuse services

promises.quote: G4S Forensic and Medical Service are responsible for the provision of medical services to Hertfordshire Police as defined in a specific contract written by Hertfordshire Police ("the Contract"), which does not at this time, provide for putting a dedicated substance misuse team into each of the police stations served by the Contract
promises.summary: No dedicated substance misuse team will be created; existing contract limits medical support to assessment and advice.

promises.quote: We do however take our duty of care for the welfare of detainees very seriously and provide medical care in custody which effectively triages our detainees to assess that they are fit to be detained and are kept safe.
promises.summary: Provide medical care in custody with triage to assess fitness and safety

concerns.quote: That was no dedicated substance misuse team available to look after Mr Broad when he was in the custody suite at Hatfield Police Station, as there would have been had Mr Broad been detained in prison
concerns.hazard: lack of dedicated substance misuse team in police custody

concerns.quote: Specially trained nursing staff should be available at hospitals for dealing with patients with substance misuse
concerns.hazard: lack of specialised nursing staff for substance misuse patients

concerns.quote: Police are required to make risk assessments and have requirements when dealing with the handcuffing of seriously ill detainees
concerns.hazard: inadequate risk assessment for seriously ill detainees

promises.quote: We feel that this represents a common sense approach, which we would suggest would ensue in the majority of circumstances, therefore we take no issue with incorporating appropriate guidance to this affect as part of the interim review of the Detention and Custody Authorised Professional Practice which is currently ongoing. We anticipate that the updated guidance will be published and available via the College website circa summer 2015.
promises.summary: Issue guidance on verbal consultation between medical practitioner and custody sergeant regarding observation levels

concerns.quote: That consideration be given to issuing guidance that whenever a detainee is attended upon by a medical practitioner there should be a verbal consultation between the medical practitioner and custody sergeant as to any issues of concern and the level of observations to be had for that detainee in addition to the medical practitioner making detailed notes on the detainee's custody medical record.
concerns.hazard: lack of verbal consultation between medical practitioner and custody sergeant regarding observation levels

concerns.quote: That consideration be given to the provision of joint training exercises for medical practitioners, custody sargeants and custody
concerns.hazard: lack of joint training for medical practitioners, custody sergeants and assistants

concerns.quote: That training should provide targeted emphasis on the correct levels of observation.
concerns.hazard: inadequate training on correct observation levels

concerns.quote: That consideration should be given to eliminating the phrase 'continue observations at the current level' and require that doctors and custody sargeants specify the level of observation precisely.
concerns.hazard: ambiguous instruction to continue observations at current level

concerns.quote: That training should include targeted training on the risks and dangers of drug and alcohol abuse, including methadone intoxication and alcohol withdrawal, particularly if the detainee is likely to be in custody for upwards of 24 hours.
concerns.hazard: lack of training on drug and alcohol risks including methadone intoxication and alcohol withdrawal

links.explanation: Both reports address insufficient handling of substance‑misuse issues among detainees in police custody. The earlier report calls for a dedicated substance‑misuse team comparable to prison care, while the later report requests targeted training on drug and alcohol risks.

links.later_quote: That training should include targeted training on the risks and dangers of drug and alcohol abuse, including methadone intoxication and alcohol withdrawal, particularly if the detainee is likely to be in custody for upwards of 24 hours.
